named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: Journal article proposing a TLE model (Trust, Language and communication, Ethics) to explain social robot technology acceptance across cultures. It argues cross-cultural trust must be calibrated with ethical values and language localisation must address symbolic systems and cultural pragmatics, offering a framework for culturally embedded AI products.
annotation.title_clean: A Study of Social Robot Technology Acceptance from the Perspective of Cultural Suitability—Construction of a TLE Model Based on Trust, Language and Ethics
annotation.title_en: A Study of Social Robot Technology Acceptance from the Perspective of Cultural Suitability—Construction of a TLE Model Based on Trust, Language and Ethics
annotation.venue: Advances in Philosophy 哲学进展
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes TLE model: trust, language and communication, ethical alignment
Developer-culture-based robot design causes cognitive bias and user resistance

Language localisation must address symbolic systems and cultural pragmatic rules
